```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Payer clarity. A names a buyer with budget authority over CI tooling, an Engineering or Platform lead. Its sourced price anchor (Harness AI add-on, $20-50/dev/month) means a single small team could produce meaningful revenue. B's payer is an individual consumer paying cents per minute, anchored to Lessrec's $0.05/min. B's own brief admits this caps pricing power.",
    "Unit economics. B's sourced acquisition benchmark (Apple Search Ads CPI of $1 to $15+) looks expensive next to per-minute revenue, and B gives no LTV evidence. A's sourced self-serve dev-tool CAC benchmark ($200-700) is plausibly recoverable at a $20-50/dev/month price point.",
    "Commoditization pressure. Both briefs describe crowded markets, but B's competitors (Lessrec, TranscribeBee, TranscribeVoice, Speechnotes) are already at the same low price, and MacWhisper offers one-time-purchase local transcription. A's sourced competition is split. Enterprise incumbents (Develocity is contact-sales only) leave a plausible self-serve SMB gap. The OSS and indie clones are described as unmonetized, which does not prove the gap is unserved but does not close it either.",
    "Demand evidence. A cites a quantified analysis of 20.2M CI jobs, plus practitioner quotes describing value in prioritizing by blocked PRs and auto-ticketing. B's quotes complain that adjacent products (Notion AI, Ultimate Brain) are too expensive, which is weak evidence of willingness to pay for a new transcription tool specifically.",
    "Feasibility in 90 days. A's brief cites several one-person OSS projects that already implement the core technique, though its six-week MVP estimate is marked unsourced and so counts as missing. A's wedge can launch as an advisory flaky-test signal rather than a merge gate, which sidesteps part of the trust and false-negative risk A's brief raises."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's seed demand signal, the 2023 HN thread, undercuts itself. The brief notes the top reply recommended MacWhisper, a one-time-purchase local tool, and that this is what the poster adopted. B's anchor evidence therefore shows the complainant solved the problem without paying per minute, which is the opposite of B's pay-as-you-go thesis. Two of B's strongest case-against claims, the free Google on-device app and Untold's free bundled transcription, carry no URLs. They are effectively unsourced and were not weighed as evidence either way.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A clearly wins on payer, price, and unit economics as evidenced. A has real sourced risks: crowded incumbents, false-negative trust requirements, and cold-start data problems. Part of its demand evidence comes from Trunk, a vendor with an interest in the problem, and its price anchor is an enterprise add-on, not proven SMB willingness to pay. Neither brief shows any evidence of a customer actually paying a new entrant, so the pick rests on structural signals rather than demonstrated traction."
}
```
